summary: Grand Canyon National Park fire tower in Coconino County, Arizona, built 1929 as a 35-foot Aermotor LS-40; inactive since at least 2009; the register and park disagree on the rim.

events.note: A fire lookout 'was established at Signal Hill' in 1926, per the Report of the Director of the National Park Service, as quoted on the Forest Lookouts Arizona page; unclear whether it is the same site as the 1929 tower
Built 1929 as a 35-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower; the register and the 2009 park page agree
Roy Lemons manned the tower in 1937, according to a July 1995 park interview quoted on the 2009 park page

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower overlooks some of the most fire-prone areas on the North Rim; the park's 2009 page places it near Pasture Wash on the South Rim. The story follows the park, which built and manages the tower. The record's coordinates were not checked against either description.

notes_for_editor: Rim conflict is unresolved by coordinates: the record's lat/lon come from the register. The 1926 'fire lookout established at Signal Hill' is second-hand, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page from a Park Service Director's report; the original was not read, and it may be the same site as the 1929 tower or an earlier one. The record's material 'steel' is inferred from the LS-40 model name; no source read says steel. Access and current condition are not verified beyond the 2009 'inactive' statement and the undated FFLA 'Standing' list. One web search was used and found no visiting information.
